figures.title: The research atlas
figures.explanation: A layered map links questions, research attempts, checked results and industrial uses. Follow one path to its evidence.
figures.interaction: Select a research stage, expose dependency paths and separate the stages; compare the four obligations. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: Original schematic. Node counts, distances and connections are explanatory, not measurements. In 3D, the four planes represent the four named stages. The highlighted path carries the same meaning in both views.
figures.validation: Each edge has a stated relationship; the same story remains legible as a 2D path.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Select a field and traverse one example; spatial depth represents named stages, not an invented quantitative variable.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Chapter claim map; original explanatory geometry.

figures.title: Capability is not access
figures.explanation: Separate demonstrated research performance, public availability, price and restrictions.
figures.interaction: Read a dated comparison of research systems, released artefacts and access boundaries.
figures.evidence_basis: Dated 9 September 2026. Based on the OpenAI Navier–Stokes announcement and Anthropic’s Fermat, zeta, protein-design and science-access announcements. No inference that a public product shares an internal configuration’s capabilities.
figures.validation: Unknown availability is marked unknown; internal results never inherit a public model label.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Select a result to reveal model, date, tools and actual availability.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S01, S03, S04, S08, S09 plus publication-date model documentation.

figures.title: What PhD-level work contains
figures.explanation: Compare literature reasoning, coding, proof, measurement analysis and experimental judgement without a single intelligence score.
figures.interaction: Compare five research tasks with their corresponding burden of proof.
figures.evidence_basis: Original analytical decomposition of research work. This is not a benchmark or a ranking of models against human researchers.
figures.validation: No exam score is silently converted into comprehensive researcher competence.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Choose a task and see the evidence and missing tests.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Task-level papers and original evaluations to be assembled.

figures.title: A vortex under scrutiny
figures.explanation: Inspect finite parametric curves and separate twisting from radial contraction; the figure does not solve a fluid equation.
figures.interaction: Adjust twist, contraction, section and filament count; switch colour encodings and inspect the linked radius profile. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: Educational parametric curves, with adjustable twist, contraction and inspection plane. Defaults: angle θ = θ₀ + 7s, radius r = 2.5(1 − 0.65s), axial coordinate y = 5s − 2.5, for 0 ≤ s ≤ 1. Arbitrary units. This drawing is not a velocity field or a numerical solution; it makes no claim about viscosity or finite-time blowup.
figures.validation: State equations, assumptions, units and sampling. Never simulate infinity or imply a rendering verifies a singularity.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Rotate, inspect a slice and scrub a finite illustrated interval.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Original explicit curve equation; S01 supplies the surrounding mathematical context.

figures.title: What has actually been checked
figures.explanation: Track announcement, paper, formal artefact and independent scrutiny as separate events.
figures.interaction: Follow dated evidence links and inspect the verification states.
figures.evidence_basis: Sources: OpenAI announcement and repository; Clay prize rules. Evidence cut-off 9 September 2026. Unresolved means not established by the evidence assembled for this essay, not that the claim is false.
figures.validation: Publication date and event date remain distinct; do not imply prize acceptance.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Open each dated item and inspect its source.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S01, S02 and independent assessment to be acquired.

figures.title: Fermat, discovery and formalisation
figures.explanation: Put the original proof and later formalisation on separate tracks.
figures.interaction: Read the historical and formalisation tracks and their source notes.
figures.evidence_basis: Wiles, Annals of Mathematics (1995); Anthropic announcement (4 September 2026); repository attribution. Timeline is schematic and does not encode elapsed time by distance.
figures.validation: The formalisation is never labelled the first human proof.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Move between contributions and source notes.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S03; original historical proof and formalisation repository to inspect.

figures.title: Inside a checked proof
figures.explanation: Show theorem dependencies and the boundary between informal statements and machine-checked claims.
figures.interaction: Inspect a bounded, real dependency slice and follow the released source.
figures.evidence_basis: Transcribed relationships from the released PROOF-PATH.md, inspected 9 September 2026. The entire repository was not rebuilt here. The upstream source is linked directly; only this bounded slice is shown.
figures.validation: Every displayed checked status corresponds to an actual artefact; indicate whether the build was independently rerun.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Expand a small real dependency tree and see the stated assumptions.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Pinned formal repository from S03; a bounded theorem slice.

figures.title: The zeta landscape
figures.explanation: Render a sampled modulus landscape of the complex zeta function with the critical line visible.
figures.interaction: Select a sampled real coordinate, imaginary interval, height exaggeration and mesh; compare untransformed magnitudes with the critical line. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: mpmath 1.3.0, 35 decimal digits. Grid: 41 real coordinates in [0,1] × 121 imaginary coordinates in [10,30]. Base height = log(1 + |ζ|), clipped at 1.8 and multiplied by the chosen display exaggeration. Pole s=1 lies outside this domain. The 2D slice uses 1,201 points. Three zero residuals and ζ(2)=π²/6 checked during generation. Data and generator are included with the article.
figures.validation: Document analytic continuation, sample domain, clipping, precision and the pole. Finite zero samples never establish the hypothesis.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Rotate, choose a slice, compare with a clear 2D view.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Independent high-precision computation; S04 for the related result.

figures.title: A stronger bound
figures.explanation: Explain the reported 41.6% to 67.2% lower-bound change with its exact meaning.
figures.interaction: Compare full-baseline lower-bound bars and read the exact qualification.
figures.evidence_basis: Anthropic announcement, original paper and expert note. Rounded values follow the announcement; the note gives approximately 67.25% with a limiting error term and precise counting conventions. Full 0–100% baseline shown.
figures.validation: No label says the conjecture is 67.2% solved; no sampled-zero percentage is substituted for the asymptotic claim.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Reveal the statement behind each bound and the unresolved question.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S04 and linked papers.

figures.title: A protein, with uncertainty
figures.explanation: Compare a benign experimental structure and a prediction, with explicit alignment and confidence annotation.
figures.interaction: Inspect any residue; superimpose or separate structures; switch confidence, displacement and sequence colour; compare backbone tubes and Cα atoms. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: Experimental PDB 1LYZ chain A residues 1–129; AlphaFold DB P00698 residues 19–147 (signal peptide excluded). All 129 residue identities verified; Cα coordinates aligned by proper-rotation least squares. Units Å. The static view colours the prediction by pLDDT; the instrument also offers aligned displacement and sequence position. Confidence is not experimental uncertainty. PDB CC0; AlphaFold CC BY 4.0. File hashes, coordinate URLs and alignment method are in protein.json.
figures.validation: Record accessions, provenance, licence, alignment and units; distinguish confidence from experimental error.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Rotate, switch between ribbon and surface, inspect a residue.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Experimental PDB 1LYZ and AlphaFold DB P00698; aligned 129-residue mature chain, with provenance in protein.json.

figures.title: The binding interface
figures.explanation: Explain how molecular shape and a measured interaction relate, using a safe documented example.
figures.interaction: Select a ligand atom, change proximity threshold, toggle neighbourhood and backbone, and inspect nearest stored-neighbour distances. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: PDB 1STP chain A and BTN ligand, CC0. Violet protein atoms lie within 4 Å of a ligand atom; the threshold marks proximity, not chemical bonds or measured affinity. The displayed chain is a selected part of the deposited structure. No AI-designed molecule is represented.
figures.validation: A plausible pose is never labelled measured affinity, efficacy or a therapeutic result.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Reveal the interface and compare representations.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Experimental PDB 1STP chain A and BTN ligand; deposited coordinates and provenance in binding.json.

figures.title: From designs to measured hits
figures.explanation: Show the actual denominators, conditions and unsuccessful cases of a selected design campaign.
figures.interaction: Compare the reported denominators and experimental-arm rates with qualification.
figures.evidence_basis: Anthropic’s August 2026 protein-design technical report and announcement. Totals and arm rates are reported observations, not independently replicated here. The inconclusive target and unequal experimental configurations are retained in the explanation.
figures.validation: Reconcile denominators and model versions; retain negative outcomes and uncertainty.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Compare experimental arms and reveal sample definitions.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S08 technical report and released results.

figures.title: Reading an instrument
figures.explanation: Demonstrate how a documented chemical measurement becomes an analytical conclusion.
figures.interaction: Inspect reported purity estimates, their difference and the stated processing time.
figures.evidence_basis: Reported values from the NMR/LC-MS technical report. Purity comparison: 96.4 − 96.33 = 0.07 percentage points. No raw spectrum has been reconstructed or fabricated. The figure deliberately shows the reported measurement comparison rather than invented peaks.
figures.validation: Do not invent peaks or measurements; mark pedagogical simplifications and any uncertainty.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Inspect labelled features and the supporting conclusion.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S08 plus reusable example measurement data.

figures.title: A crystal before it is a product
figures.explanation: A rotatable unit cell connects predicted structure to stability, synthesis and use.
figures.interaction: Replicate conventional cells, move the reveal plane, inspect nearest-neighbour links and distinguish the two carbon sublattices. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: COD 9008564 revision 291735, Wyckoff (1963), via AMCSD. Cell length 3.56679 Å. Origin site expanded using the CIF’s explicit symmetry operations; eight unique periodic sites per conventional cell; 18 boundary-inclusive sites in one cell. Repeated blocks deduplicate shared boundaries. Links mark nearest neighbours. CC0 data; source CIF and generator included.
figures.validation: Predicted stability, synthesis and commercial utility remain distinct.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Inspect the cell and switch between documented evidence states.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S12 and a released CIF with suitable reuse terms.

figures.title: The algorithm that earns its keep
figures.explanation: Compare a selected algorithm with the relevant baseline under stated conditions.
figures.interaction: Compare scalar-multiplication counts and inspect the independently checked identity.
figures.evidence_basis: Published AlphaEvolve rank-48 tensor for 4×4 complex matrix multiplication; recursive Strassen baseline 49. All 4,096 entries checked from literal coefficient data without executing the downloaded notebook. Gaussian half-integer coefficients scaled by two for exact bounded arithmetic. This is an identity check, not a hardware benchmark.
figures.validation: Use compatible units and hardware; distinguish reproduced measurements from reported ones.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Switch metric or problem size without changing the underlying comparison.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S10/S11; published benchmark and reproducible code.

figures.title: Where feedback is fast
figures.explanation: Compare proof checking, software tests, physical experiments and clinical outcomes.
figures.interaction: Compare research fields and the evaluators they require.
figures.evidence_basis: Original analytical comparison grounded in the mathematical, algorithmic, materials, protein and clinical sources in chapters 2–6. Qualitative stages, not measured durations or a universal ranking of research speed.
figures.validation: Do not manufacture comparable timings where only qualitative evidence exists.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Select a type of research to inspect its feedback process.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Case dossiers across mathematics, computing, materials and biology.

figures.title: The small lab, expanded
figures.explanation: Show a research work queue branching into attempts, merging duplicated ideas and feeding a limited checker.
figures.interaction: Change population, distinctness, checking capacity and assumed acceptance; inspect the throughput plateau and queued candidates. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: Original accounting scenario: one attempt per agent per day; uniqueness, checking capacity and acceptance are user-controlled, with defaults of 25%, 500 checks/day and 20%. Expected counts are illustrative. 3D dots are aggregate schematic groups, not individual agents or measured discoveries; the numerical flow is provided in 2D.
figures.validation: Aggregate large populations; render no fake live agents. State throughput, correlation and saturation assumptions.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Vary a scenario from a few workers to a million; inspect accepted outputs and capacity limits.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Original transparent scenario model informed by S18.

figures.title: More agents, less certainty
figures.explanation: Show where coordination helps and where repeated errors or overhead erase gains.
figures.interaction: Compare the dated study outcomes and independently vary the correlation illustration.
figures.evidence_basis: Study panel: Kim et al., arXiv:2512.08296v3, 260 configurations, six benchmarks. Separate illustration: effective sample size n/[1+(n−1)ρ] for the variance of an equicorrelated mean with equal marginal variances. Not calibrated to agents, not a success-rate or discovery prediction.
figures.validation: Keep observed results separate from extrapolation; no curve pretends to measure a million agents.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Compare published study conditions, then separately explore assumptions.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S18 and released code.

figures.title: The cost of a checked result
figures.explanation: Break total research cost into inference, tools, evaluation, human review and experiments.
figures.interaction: Vary inference and physical-test costs in a disclosed fixed-population scenario.
figures.evidence_basis: Original illustrative USD accounting, not current commercial pricing. Fixed 1,000 attempts, 25% uniqueness, $2/check, 20% initial acceptance. Costs of physical tests are included but their success is not assumed. All omitted costs are disclosed. Inputs and sums are reproducible in scenarios.ts.
figures.validation: Label cost units, retries and omissions; do not compare inference price directly with a fully loaded R&D budget.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Change visible inputs and compare small-lab and incumbent cases.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Public prices and measured workloads to collect; original cost model.

figures.title: Who can actually use it
figures.explanation: Show access conditions and practical barriers without implying equal opportunity everywhere.
figures.interaction: Select one of six sampled countries; inspect dated API listings and the accessible table.
figures.evidence_basis: Six sampled countries checked against official OpenAI and Anthropic API country lists on 9 September 2026. Country markers are approximate label locations, not individual users. Natural Earth public-domain land, equirectangular projection. Grey regions are unassessed. The map does not represent all providers, model capabilities, affordability or restrictions.
figures.validation: Unknown regions stay unknown; a language capability is not inferred from interface availability.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Select a country and inspect dated source-backed availability.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Official service country lists, terms, prices, connectivity and income data to assemble.

figures.title: A research programme outside the centre
figures.explanation: Trace one real non-elite or geographically remote research workflow and the resources it required.
figures.interaction: Read a clearly hypothetical engineering workflow and its dependencies.
figures.evidence_basis: Explicit hypothetical engineering workflow. No invented person, quotation, field measurement or commercial outcome. The stages identify where digital assistance and local knowledge can complement facilities and independent assessment.
figures.validation: If no adequate case exists, use an explicitly labelled scenario with no implied reporting.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Follow steps and reveal what was provided, rented or unavailable.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: A verified public case must be identified; no invented person or quotation.

figures.title: What the university still does
figures.explanation: Separate teaching, research, verification, facilities, credentials and public goods.
figures.interaction: Select a university function; compare the changing task and institutional contribution.
figures.evidence_basis: Original institutional analysis, not a numerical exposure ranking. The six functions are discussed in chapter 9 with examples of public educational and research infrastructure.
figures.validation: Label analytical judgements; support each allegation about a named institution.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Inspect evidence of exposure and adaptation for each function.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: University policies, budgets and measured cases to research.

figures.title: The public work beneath the model
figures.explanation: Link original papers, public data, open tools, institutions and later AI results.
figures.interaction: Follow two selected contribution chains with stated attribution limits.
figures.evidence_basis: Selected chains based on the Fermat repository attribution, Lean documentation, AlphaFold and RFdiffusion papers and public structural databases. Arrows indicate contribution, not exclusive causation. This is not a complete intellectual genealogy.
figures.validation: Avoid implying that AI developed its scientific foundations independently.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Follow a contribution chain and inspect attribution.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Source lineage from S03-S13 and original repositories.

figures.title: Take the R&D department apart
figures.explanation: Separate literature work, modelling, experiments, testing, fabrication and deployment.
figures.interaction: Compare four research stages, digital assistance, complementary assets and acceptance tests.
figures.evidence_basis: Original task decomposition. Qualitative relationships, not measured automation percentages. Company evidence and distinctions are developed in chapters 10 and 11.
figures.validation: No arbitrary percentage of R&D is labelled automatable.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Compare a smaller lab and an incumbent against the same output.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Company case dossiers; S15-S17 as starting sources.

figures.title: Win one valuable piece
figures.explanation: Show how a challenger can sell a component, research service or specialised tool within an existing value chain.
figures.interaction: Select a commercial entry point to see buyer, promise, test, dependency and possible outcome.
figures.evidence_basis: Three explicit commercial scenarios. No company, transaction, revenue or market-share outcome is claimed as observed. Dependencies and acceptance tests remain visible.
figures.validation: No assumed revenue or market share masquerades as observed displacement.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Choose an entry point and inspect its dependencies and possible buyer.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Documented market structure plus labelled scenarios.

figures.title: The machine and its measurements
figures.explanation: Use simplified metrology geometry to explain why computation and physical precision are complementary.
figures.interaction: Change synthetic translation, rotation and distortion; compare before and after correction with linked RMS and sample profiles. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: Original educational geometry in arbitrary units, informed by ASML’s public computational-lithography and measuring-accuracy explanations. Not a proprietary EUV layout, ray-tracing simulation or calibrated instrument model. The drawn path explains observation, not a specific optical architecture.
figures.validation: Label educational geometry; do not claim a faithful proprietary EUV digital twin.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Rotate, reveal a measurement path and inspect sources of error.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S15 and official ASML technical explanations to acquire.

figures.title: The motor that survives the workshop
figures.explanation: Explore the geometry and trade-offs of a generic motor study tied to a documented engineering example.
figures.interaction: Explode the assembly, rotate the rotor and toggle housing, cutaway and windings; inspect engineering obligations without invented performance. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: Original generic geometry: six stator regions, central rotor, shaft and housing, arbitrary dimensions. No Dyson design, material parameters, field solution, efficiency or performance simulation is represented. Dyson’s engineering descriptions provide context only.
figures.validation: Simulation settings and assumed material properties are explicit; never label it a Dyson product model.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Rotate and inspect alternatives with tested or explicitly illustrative performance.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S17 context; open engineering model and validation source to select.

figures.title: Four research advantages, examined
figures.explanation: Compare ASML, IBM, Google and Dyson on intellectual work, data, facilities, integration and customers.
figures.interaction: Compare four companies in a single evidence-and-scenario matrix.
figures.evidence_basis: Company primary sources: ASML 2025 report and technical explanations; IBM’s December 2024 materials-model release; Google DeepMind’s AlphaEvolve publications; Dyson’s research and motor-engineering descriptions. Challenger entries and responses are the essay’s analysis, not company forecasts.
figures.validation: No invented moat score or claim that all four are passive incumbents.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Select a company to reveal evidence, challenger opportunities and incumbent responses.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: S10/S11, S15-S17 plus completed company dossiers.

figures.title: Below the oilfield
figures.explanation: Reveal a reservoir cross-section and uncertainty across plausible subsurface interpretations.
figures.interaction: Move the section and well, blend geometries, change vertical exaggeration and switch sedimentary block versus horizons; inspect unexaggerated profiles. All 3D views include three guided states, reset, 50–200% magnification, zoom buttons, touch pinch, named camera views, rotation, labels, lighting, expansion, saved-readout comparison, shareable controls and JSON/PNG export.
figures.evidence_basis: Synthetic educational surfaces: y = 1.2 − 1.15l + 0.28 sin(0.65x) cos(0.7z) + 0.7a exp[−(x²+z²)/7], layers l=0…3, alternative a∈[0,1], x∈[−4,4], z∈[−3,3]. Arbitrary units. The 3D surface uses 65×33 vertices per horizon; solid cut faces add procedural bedding and grain. The linked profile contains 161 points at the selected section z; the static explanation uses z=0. No field observations, permeability, pressure, reserves or flow calculation. Both geometries are invented, not statistically fitted alternatives.
figures.validation: State geometry, units and provenance; show uncertainty rather than invented operational forecasts.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Rotate, slice and compare alternative models.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Original analytic four-horizon model; procedural sedimentary materials, explicitly synthetic.

figures.title: Five industrial futures
figures.explanation: Compare oil and gas, pharma, manufacturing, utilities and software/services with the same seven questions.
figures.interaction: Select one of exactly five industries and inspect the same seven questions; compare all five.
figures.evidence_basis: Explicit scenarios grounded in chapters 5, 11 and 12 and their primary sources. The table is an analytical comparison, not a forecast or a ranking. No probabilities or dates of displacement are assigned.
figures.validation: Exactly five sectors; each includes benefits, remaining constraints and measurable progress indicators.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Select a sector and compare challenger entry, incumbent adoption and customer benefit.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: five-industry-futures.md; each future grounded in its case dossier.

figures.title: From an idea to an improvement
figures.explanation: Connect research assistance to validation, implementation and customer benefit across the five sectors.
figures.interaction: Vary candidate arrivals, validation capacity and deployment capacity; inspect both queues.
figures.evidence_basis: Original one-period deterministic accounting. Validated = min(arrivals, validation capacity); deployed = min(validated, deployment capacity). Empty initial queues and all processed candidates pass. Candidates are interchangeable units; actual sectoral workflows contain rejection, feedback and unequal work. Not an empirical productivity forecast.
figures.validation: Faster idea generation cannot automatically shorten every downstream stage.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Change a constrained stage and see where a queue shifts.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Original explicit process model, calibrated only where evidence permits.

figures.title: The clocks that remain
figures.explanation: Compare scientific work, testing, clinical or industrial validation and deployment times.
figures.interaction: Vary the accelerated share and stage speedup in a serial elapsed-time scenario.
figures.evidence_basis: Serial two-stage accounting on a 100-unit baseline: T = 100(1−f) + 100f/s, where f is the accelerated share and s its speedup. No actual industry duration is represented. Fixed scope, no overlap, queue, rework or change in the other stage. Not a clinical or industrial schedule.
figures.validation: No unsourced universal times; distinguish elapsed time from staff hours.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Choose a workflow and inspect the source for each duration.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Trials, manufacturing qualification and deployment records to research.

figures.title: Who receives the savings
figures.explanation: Trace a lower research cost into prices, profits, entry and additional demand.
figures.interaction: Vary research cost share, cost reduction and pass-through; inspect reconciled prices and margins.
figures.evidence_basis: Original accounting scenario: baseline price 100, cost 80. Saving = 80 × research share × reduction; customer saving = saving × pass-through. New cost + unit margin + customer saving = 100. Abstract units, fixed volume and quality; no observed company costs or forecast market shares.
figures.validation: Totals reconcile; no made-up market forecasts; keep baseline and counterfactual visible.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Vary cost reduction and pass-through assumptions.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Company cost and pricing evidence to gather; transparent accounting model.

figures.title: The timing of market change
figures.explanation: Separate scientific progress, deployment, customer adoption and market response.
figures.interaction: Switch between fewer and more adoption barriers; inspect conditional sequences.
figures.evidence_basis: Two qualitative scenarios developed in chapter 14. No dates, probabilities or universal industry-collapse sequence. Distances in the diagram do not encode measured time.
figures.validation: No promised date for industry collapse; distinguish announcement effects from operating results.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Compare faster and slower adoption assumptions.
figures.planned_evidence_basis: Dated case histories and labelled scenarios.

figures.title: The dependency moves
figures.explanation: Map access to models, compute, data, experiments and distribution.
figures.interaction: Select a dependency and follow the corresponding evidence or analysis.
figures.evidence_basis: Original qualitative network. Provider country lists, EuroHPC access, UNESCO open-science principles and the industry analysis establish different parts of the context. Edges indicate necessary relationships, not ownership shares or measured market concentration.
figures.validation: Do not confuse public use with public ownership or control.
figures.fallback: Accessible static figure, HTML caption and method/source note; table or 2D view where appropriate.
figures.planned_interaction: Trace a small lab and an incumbent through the same dependencies.
